content: The preferences dialog in MediaWiki allows users to customize certain aspects of their experience on the platform. These settings are only applied when the user is logged in. The default system administrator login name is WikiSysop. Some MediaWiki projects are part of a family, meaning a single login applies across all projects in the family, and shared preference settings are used. This is particularly true for over 1,000 Wikia projects. However, on Wikimedia projects, logging in and setting preferences must be done separately for each wiki. Users may choose to set the same preferences across multiple wikis, but this is not mandatory. For more information, refer to the Single sign-on transition. User Data Email Address: Users can optionally register their email address, which will not be publicly displayed. This enables password recovery via the Mail me a new password option on the login screen. Additionally, other registered users can send emails through the Email this user link on the user page unless the user disables this feature. Disable Email from Other Users: If this option is selected, other users will not be able to send emails using the Email this user feature. Nickname Nickname vs. Username: While the username may not necessarily be the user's real name, the term nickname here refers to an optional name that can be specified for use in signatures (e.g., when using `~~~` or `~~~~`). Raw Signatures: Users can create more versatile signatures by enabling Raw signatures. This allows the use of custom text, wiki markup, and HTML in signatures. If Raw signatures is unchecked, the software automatically escapes any characters that would otherwise constitute wiki or HTML markup. If enabled, users can include links, font tags, images, and templates in their signatures. Invalid Raw Signatures: If invalid HTML markup is used in a signature, an error message may appear. Common issues include improper use of images or templates in signatures. Changes to templates or images used in signatures are retroactive, which can be confusing but also convenient for fixing problematic signatures. To avoid retroactivity, use unique template or image names. Password Changing Passwords: To change a password, users must enter their old password, the new password, and confirm the new password. This is not required when changing other preferences. Remember Password Across Sessions: Enabling this feature stores an HTTP cookie in the browser, allowing automatic login on subsequent visits. If the password was system-generated and emailed, it must be changed to use this feature. Interface Language Language Settings: Users can specify an interface language different from the wiki's default language. This affects default messages but not custom labels in the MediaWiki namespace. Some interface elements may not work correctly in certain language configurations, such as reversed tick boxes in right-to-left (RTL) projects. Skin Skin Options: MediaWiki offers various skins (e.g., Classic, Nostalgia, Cologne Blue, MonoBook). Each skin has unique HTML structures and styles. The default skin is MonoBook. Some skins, like Cologne Blue, have fixed font sizes, which may not respect browser settings. Users can also provide their own CSS to customize the appearance further. Rendering Math Math Rendering Options: Users can control how mathematical equations written in TeX code are rendered. Options include always rendering as PNG, using HTML for simple equations, or leaving the code as TeX for text-based browsers. Modern browsers are recommended for optimal rendering. Date Format Customizing Date Formats: Users can choose how dates are displayed, affecting signatures and other date-related elements. However, this setting does not retroactively change existing dates in signatures. Time Zone Time Zone Settings: Users can set their time zone by specifying the offset from UTC. This affects timestamps displayed on pages. Users observing daylight saving time must update their settings manually. Editing Editing Preferences: Users can configure the dimensions of the editing textbox, enable section editing via links or right-clicking, and choose to edit pages on double-click. Additional options include showing the edit toolbar, displaying previews above the edit box, and automatically adding created or edited pages to the watchlist. Recent Changes and Stub Display Recent Changes Settings: Users can customize the number of changes displayed, hide minor edits, and enable enhanced recent changes grouping by article. Stub display thresholds can also be adjusted. Search Result Settings Search Preferences: Users can specify the number of search results per page, the number of lines of context shown per result, and the default namespaces to search. Miscellaneous Settings Hoverbox Over Links: Users can enable or disable hoverboxes displaying link titles. Underline Links: Users can choose whether links are underlined, though browser compatibility may vary. Broken Links Formatting: Internal links to non-existent pages are displayed differently, typically underlined and in red. Notes Changing Usernames: To change a username retroactively (so that previous contributions are recorded under the new name), users must request this from a bureaucrat. Signatures and other occurrences of the old name on talk pages are not automatically updated. Account deletion is not possible. Users can provide personal information on their user page if desired.
